context: small plant · burner, dryer and bitumen system; emissions permit and mix approval govern

brief.intro: New to this project type? An asphalt plant dries and heats aggregates in a rotating drum fired by a burner, screens and weighs them, and mixes them with hot bitumen to make the asphalt laid on roads. Around the drum are cold-feed bins, a tall mixing tower, heated bitumen tanks, a filler silo, a bag-house filter that cleans the exhaust, and hot storage silos that load trucks. Like a concrete plant it arrives in modules and is erected in weeks. The programme is set by the environmental permit (it has a chimney and a burner), the fuel and bitumen supply arrangements, the foundations, and — at the end — burner tuning, emission tests and approval of the asphalt mixes by the road authority.

must_get_right: The environmental permit (emissions, noise, distance from housing) is the first activity and can decide the site itself.
Bitumen and fuel storage need bunds, heating and fire protection — design and approve them with the civil works.
Heat-up is slow: bitumen tanks and thermal oil need days to reach temperature before any hot test.
The plant earns nothing until the road authority approves the job-mix formula; plan trial mixes and laboratory tests as real activities.

basis_of_planning.standard: AACE Recommended Practice 38R-06 — Documenting the Schedule Basis

sections.heading: Scheduling method & tools
sections.body: A Critical Path Method (CPM) network built in Primavera P6, developed to a Level 3 control schedule with retained-logic progress. Activities are organised by plant area along the process line and by discipline, with every long-lead machine tracked from order to factory test, shipping and arrival.

sections.heading: Calendars & working time
sections.body: Standard site calendar for construction; equipment installation may run extended shifts under vendor supervision. Commissioning follows the vendor's programme, and hot commissioning runs continuously once started.

sections.heading: Sequencing logic & critical path
sections.body: Permit and supplier drawings → foundations, bunds and yard → plant erection → fuel, power and air → cold run → heat-up → burner tuning → trial mixes → emission test and mix approval. The critical path runs through the permit and plant delivery, then the approvals.

sections.heading: Key assumptions
sections.body: The process technology and vendor are fixed before design starts; vendor drawings for foundations arrive on the agreed dates; permanent power and water are available before cold commissioning; raw material for trial production is on site.

sections.heading: Access, resource & site constraints
sections.body: Heavy machines need crane access and often must enter before the cladding or a wall is closed. Vendor supervisors are booked for fixed periods. Clean, dry, powered conditions are required before precision equipment is unpacked.

sections.heading: Risks, float & contingency
sections.body: Main risks: permit refusal or conditions, fuel-supply connection, burner and emission problems, and mix approval. Contingency is held before the first paving contract date.

sections.heading: Schedule levels of detail
sections.body: Reported at Level 1 (milestones) and Level 2 (summary) to the client; controlled at Level 3 by plant area and discipline; expanded to Level 4–5 lookahead for the installation crews and the vendor supervisors — consistent with AACE 37R-06.
